description:
MEASURED s473v (2026-09-16), main 2ac855aa, gen v2-1460.  Member 1 of the
round-33 brief: the four breakdowns, taken BEFORE any lever, so the lever is
picked by the table and not by the suspicion the brief carried.

METHOD.  Each bench program is the row's own source, extracted from
tools/bench-exec.pl (scratch/s473v/mkprog.pl) so the profiled program is
byte-identical to the benched one; compiled to a fasl against this tree's
cached core and loaded under sb-sprof :cpu (scratch/s473v/{prof,runprof}.pl),
N chosen for >= 2000 samples.  Allocation is measured exactly, not sampled:
the program is loaded twice at two N and (sb-ext:get-bytes-consed) subtracted
(scratch/s473v/{bytes.lisp,runbytes.pl}) -- the same cancellation bench-exec
does for time.  Box shared with a sibling agent, load average 2.2-3.0; the
SHARES are what the tables are read for, not the wall times.

BENCH BEFORE (BENCH_K=5, load avg 3.04 at the end of the run):

    bench          perl(s)     pcl(s)  pcl/perl
    strcat          0.3158     0.6744     2.14x
    sortnum         0.0269     0.0707     2.63x
    sortstr         0.0744     0.1150     1.55x
    feread          0.5093     0.1282     0.25x   (control)
    json-rt         0.9736     1.7149     1.76x
    textproc        0.4942     1.5678     3.17x
    regexg          0.4117     0.8985     2.18x
    subste          0.0578     0.2762     4.78x

regexg = 6 M matches of /./g: 150 ns per match against perl's 69.

=== TABLE 1: regexg (N=70 = 14 M matches of /./g, ZERO capture groups) ======
2145 samples / 2.145 s.  Self %, grouped:

    group                                                     self %
    ENGINE  cl-ppcre scanner closure 18.7 + matcher 2.5        21.2
    do-regex-match self                                        12.6
    set-match-vars 7.7 + %p-at-elem-set 7.3
      + vector-hairy-data-vector-ref 2.1 + %set-fill-pointer 0.5   17.6   <- @-/@+
    hash-table-count (FOUR calls per match: %+ and %- twice)     5.6
    length (ONE call per /g step, on an already-simple subject)  5.0
    set-capture-groups self (TWENTY generic > on num-groups=0)   4.9
    clear-capture-groups 4.1 + %clear-match-strings 1.4          5.5
    wrapper: top level form 4.6, p-=~ 2.1, %p-true-p-slow 2.2,
      RETURN-MULTIPLE 2.2, to-string 1.4, box-sv 0.9, unbox 0.9  14.3
    generic arithmetic (two-arg->= 2.9, GENERIC-< 1.5, = + 0.4)   4.8
    pos table: gethash/eq-hash/flat 1.3 + puthash 1.5             2.8
    %p-regex-compiled                                             2.4
    optimized-data-vector-ref t                                   1.4

    THE EAGER MATCH-VARIABLE TRIO = 17.6 + 5.6 + 4.9 + 5.5 = 33.6 %
    -- on a pattern with NO capture groups at all.

ALLOCATION: 20.8 bytes per OUTER iteration = 200 000 matches, i.e. ~0.0001
bytes per match.  The eager path allocates NOTHING per match (that is #680's
reused @-/@+ boxes).  CONSTRAINT ON ANY FIX: a per-match record must not
allocate either -- a struct per match would be a regression.

=== TABLE 2: subste (N=25000; 20 short fields x s/([aeiou])/uc($1)/ge + s/\s+/_/g)
2084 samples / 2.084 s.  ONE capture group, and $1 IS read (in the /e side).

    group                                                     self %
    ENGINE + cl-ppcre replace machinery: scanner closure 7.7,
      char-class test fn 3.4, matcher closures 2.6+2.5,
      replace-aux 2.4, regex-replace-all 1.7, build-replacement 1.7,
      whitespacep 0.9, store-end-of-reg 0.6                     23.5
    CLOS DISPATCH on cl-ppcre:scan -- fast-method 2.0, emf 1.3,
      check-applicable-keywords 2.2, dlisp3 lambdas 2.1          7.6   <- see below
    set-match-vars 4.0 (total 16.2 with at-elem-set + hairy aref
      + the $+ / $^N subseqs)
    set-capture-groups 2.3 (total 9.4 -- the @{^CAPTURE} box per group)
    clear-capture-groups 1.8 (total 7.5, of which `set` on a capture
      SYMBOL is 4.2: about-to-modify-symbol-value + %lookup-symbol
      + packed-info-value-index + get-info-value)
    ub32-bash-copy 4.0, string-sout 3.3, %write-string 1.7,
      get-output-stream-string 1.9 (cl-ppcre builds the result string)
    vector-hairy-data-vector-ref 3.3, vector-subseq 2.3
    do-regex-subst self 2.0 (total 94.7)

    THE EAGER TRIO (set-match-vars 16.2 + set-capture-groups 9.4
    + clear-capture-groups 7.5, overlapping the hairy/subseq rows) = ~33 %,
    and the program reads exactly ONE of the variables it fills ($1).

ALLOCATION: 76 035 bytes per outer iteration = ~160 matches, ~475 bytes per
match -- cl-ppcre's result string plus, per match, the @{^CAPTURE} box, the
$1 subseq, the $+ subseq and the $^N subseq (three subseqs where one is read).

FINDING, not a lever this round: `cl-ppcre:scan` is called GENERICALLY by
cl-ppcre's own regex-replace-all (and by cl-ppcre:split -- 7.7 % of textproc
through the same four frames).  %p-ppcre-scan (#680) removed exactly this cost
for m//, and s/// does not go through it because the scan is inside
regex-replace-all.  Filed as #1808.

=== TABLE 3: textproc (N=700) ==============================================
2803 samples / 2.803 s.

    ENGINE: scanner closure 10.4 + char-searcher 7.6 + bmh matcher 3.5  21.5
    do-regex-match self 5.1 (total 58.8)
    set-match-vars 4.7 (total 16.3) + %p-at-elem-set 2.9
      + vector-hairy-data-vector-ref 2.4                                10.0
    length 2.9, hash-table-count 2.6
    set-capture-groups 2.3 (total 6.2), clear-capture-groups 1.7 (5.6)
    CLOS dispatch on cl-ppcre:scan 7.7 total (reached through cl-ppcre:split,
      11.2 % total)
    ub8-bash-copy 2.1, box-set 1.9, p-string-concat 1.8,
      %concatenate-to-string 4.6 total, replace 2.2 total

    THE EAGER TRIO ~ 28 %.  textproc's inner `$s++ while $l =~ /o/g` is
    regexg's shape (zero groups) and its outer match has ONE group.

ALLOCATION: 3 512 588 bytes per outer iteration over 2000 lines = 1757 bytes
per line.

=== TABLE 4: json-rt (N=150) ===============================================
3152 samples / 3.152 s.  THE ROW THAT SAYS NO.

    JSON::PP's own subs (the module-cache lambdas) dominate; do-regex-match is
    15.9 % TOTAL with 2.3 % self, do-regex-subst 9.1 % total, and
    set-match-vars / set-capture-groups / clear-capture-groups DO NOT APPEAR
    IN THE PROFILE AT ALL (not one sample in 3152).

    The reason is the shape: JSON::PP's hot regexes are FAILED matches (the
    encoder's escape s/// finds nothing in ordinary text), and the eager trio
    runs only on SUCCESS.  So json-rt's regex time is ENGINE time -- the
    char-class test function 7.8 % + the scanner closure 6.4 % + the matchers
    2.3 % -- which is #71's territory and USER-parked.

    json-rt is therefore NOT a target for the match-record lever, and the
    round says so up front rather than measuring a disappointment later.
    What IS in json-rt besides the engine: box-set 2.6, %p-str-eq-slow 2.5,
    to-string 2.4, ub32-bash-copy 2.0, %make-p-box 1.6, unbox 1.6,
    p-flatten-args 1.6, %concatenate-to-string 1.5, p-find-overload 1.5 --
    a flat profile with no single lever in it.

=== WHAT THE TABLES CHOSE ==================================================
(a) THE MATCH RECORD -- ships.  33.6 % of regexg, ~33 % of subste, ~28 % of
    textproc, 0 % of json-rt.  The derived variables (@-, @+, $+, $^N,
    @{^CAPTURE}, %+, %-) materialise on READ; $1..$20 stay eager (they are
    the ones programs actually read, and the emitter reads them as bare
    symbols).  Task #1804.
(b) pos -- MEASURED AND DECLINED as a lever: the whole *p-match-pos* traffic
    on regexg is gethash 1.3 % + puthash 1.5 % = 2.8 %, which is the CEILING
    of what a one-entry cache in front of the table could win.  Under the
    20 % bar; the accessor-funnel half is not worth its own sweep either.
    Recorded here so it is not re-derived.
(c) the per-CALL coercion of a non-simple subject -- NOT MEASURABLE on these
    rows: every subject in all four is already a simple string, so the
    coercion is one simple-string-p test (to-string is 1.4 % on regexg,
    which is the unboxing, not a copy).  #1187 closed the same question from
    the other side (there is no non-simple operand; the generic accesses are
    cl-ppcre declaiming *string* as a union type).  Not built.
(d) s///'s per-call protocol -- the table puts 7.6 % in the CLOS dispatch on
    cl-ppcre:scan, below the 20 % bar for its own lever but worth a task:
    #1808.

RE-MEASURE RECIPE: scratch/s473v/{mkprog,runprof,runbytes}.pl in this
worktree; the raw reports are scratch/s473v/prof/*.txt.
subject: PERF ROUND 33 MEASUREMENT: where the per-MATCH time goes on regexg / subste / textproc / json-rt (the four profile tables the round's levers were chosen from)
